multiRename.title: Multi-rename

@multiRename.title.description: Title of the Multi-Rename Tool sheet (Ctrl+M), which renames many files at once with a name mask, like Total Commander's tool of the same name.

multiRename.scope.selection: {count, plural, one {{countText} selected file} other {{countText} selected files}}

@multiRename.scope.selection.description: Shown in the Multi-rename sheet’s title bar, after the tool’s name (multiRename.title), in quieter text: the sheet renames the files and folders the user selected. Pairs with multiRename.scope.wholeFolder, so the two must read clearly different.

placeholders.countText: how many files and folders are selected, ready to drop into the sentence (for example 1,234)

multiRename.scope.wholeFolder: {count, plural, one {The only file in this folder (nothing selected)} other {All {countText} files in this folder (nothing selected)}}

@multiRename.scope.wholeFolder.description: Shown in the Multi-rename sheet’s title bar, after the tool’s name (multiRename.title), in quieter text: nothing was selected, so the sheet works on every file and folder in the current folder. Nothing is renamed until the user presses Rename, but users who expected “only my selection” must see at a glance that it’s the whole folder. Pairs with multiRename.scope.selection.

placeholders.countText: how many files and folders the current folder holds, ready to drop into the sentence (for example 1,234)

@multiRename.nameMask.description: Label of the field holding the rename mask for the file name: plain text plus placeholders in brackets such as [N] (old name) or [C] (counter).

@multiRename.extensionMask.description: Label of the field holding the rename mask for the file extension, kept separate so a typo can't break the file type. [E] keeps the old extension.

@multiRename.insertPlaceholder.description: Accessible name of the row of buttons that insert a placeholder such as [N] or [C] into the name mask at the caret.

@multiRename.mediaButton.description: Label of the button after the placeholder buttons ([N], [E], [P], [C], [YMD]) that opens the field picker: photo, video, and music information (date taken, camera, artist, title, …) to put in the new name. Lowercase in English to sit quietly beside the bracket placeholders; follow your language's normal capitalization (a language that capitalizes nouns does so here). Don't add a ▾: the chip draws its own after the word. Keep it short: the row is tight, and a long word is cut off with an ellipsis.

@multiRename.mediaButtonName.description: Accessible name of the “media ▾” button (multiRename.mediaButton), read by screen readers and voice control: it opens the list of photo, video, and music fields. Must contain the button's visible word (multiRename.mediaButton), so a voice-control user can say it.

@multiRename.search.description: Label of the search field of the rename tool's search & replace. Supports * and ? wildcards and a|b|c lists.

@multiRename.replace.description: Label of the replacement field of the rename tool's search & replace. With a list search, x|y|z pairs up with it.

@multiRename.caseSensitive.description: Search & replace option: only match the same uppercase/lowercase letters.

@multiRename.firstOnly.description: Search & replace option: replace only the first match in each name, not all of them.

@multiRename.includeExtension.description: Search & replace option: also search and replace in the file extension.

@multiRename.regex.description: Search & replace option: the search is a regular expression; $1, $2 in the replacement insert its groups.

@multiRename.substitute.description: Search & replace option: when the search matches, the whole name becomes the replacement (Total Commander's "Subst.").

@multiRename.searchOptions.description: In the Multi-rename sheet, the accessible name of the row of small toggle chips beside the search fields that turn the search options on and off (Match case, First match only, Include extension, Regular expression, Replace whole name).

@multiRename.searchOptionHelp.setup.description: In the Multi-rename sheet, each search option (Match case, First match only, Include extension, Regular expression, Replace whole name) is a small toggle chip beside the search fields. Its tooltip names the option, shows its keyboard shortcut, and gives a tiny worked example: a replace on a made-up file name, with the result when the option is on and when it's off. This line sets up the example: what is searched for, what replaces it, and the file name it runs on. Keep the <code> tags around the three placeholders: they show in a code font.

placeholders.name: a made-up file name (e.g. Photo photo.jpg)

@multiRename.searchOptionHelp.on.description: In the Multi-rename sheet, each search option (Match case, First match only, Include extension, Regular expression, Replace whole name) is a small toggle chip beside the search fields. Its tooltip names the option, shows its keyboard shortcut, and gives a tiny worked example: a replace on a made-up file name, with the result when the option is on and when it's off. Labels the line showing the new name with the option turned on. Keep it as short as possible.

@multiRename.searchOptionHelp.off.description: In the Multi-rename sheet, each search option (Match case, First match only, Include extension, Regular expression, Replace whole name) is a small toggle chip beside the search fields. Its tooltip names the option, shows its keyboard shortcut, and gives a tiny worked example: a replace on a made-up file name, with the result when the option is on and when it's off. Labels the line showing the new name with the option turned off. Keep it as short as possible.

@multiRename.case.description: Label of the menu that changes the letter case of the new names, applied after search & replace.

@multiRename.case.unchanged.description: Letter-case menu option: keep the letter case as it is.

@multiRename.case.lower.description: Letter-case menu option: all letters lowercase. Written in lowercase on purpose, to show the result. Show-the-result labels like this one are exempt from sentence case: write them in the case they produce. In a script without letter case (Chinese, Japanese, Korean), describe the transform instead.

@multiRename.case.upper.description: Letter-case menu option: all letters uppercase. Written in uppercase on purpose, to show the result. Show-the-result labels like this one are exempt from sentence case: write them in the case they produce. In a script without letter case (Chinese, Japanese, Korean), describe the transform instead.

@multiRename.case.firstUpper.description: Letter-case menu option: the first letter of the name uppercase, the rest lowercase.

@multiRename.case.words.description: Letter-case menu option: the first letter of every word uppercase, the rest lowercase. Written that way on purpose, to show the result. Show-the-result labels like this one are exempt from sentence case: write them in the case they produce. In a script without letter case (Chinese, Japanese, Korean), describe the transform instead.

@multiRename.removeDiacritics.description: Option: turn letters with accents and other diacritics into plain letters (á becomes a, ž becomes z, ß becomes ss), in every language. An everyday word for "accents" is fine, even though ß becoming ss goes beyond diacritics. Keep this identical to multiRename.preset.removeDiacritics, the preset with the same effect.

@multiRename.greekToLatin.description: Checkbox that writes Greek letters in Latin ones, the way Greek passports do (ELOT 743): Αθήνα becomes Athina.

@multiRename.normalizeUnicode.description: Checkbox that renames names whose accented letters are stored as a letter plus a separate accent mark (as macOS and network drives often store them) to the single-character form Windows, Linux, and websites expect. The names look the same before and after.

multiRename.presets.title: Presets

@multiRename.presets.title.description: Label of the button at the bottom left of the Multi-rename tool that opens the menu of presets (saved rename settings), and the accessible name of that menu. Followed by a down arrow and, when one is loaded, the preset's name.

@multiRename.presets.edited.description: Shown on the Presets button after the loaded preset's name once the user changed a field, so the fields no longer match the preset. {preset} is the preset's name.

@multiRename.presets.tooltip.description: Tooltip of the Presets button in the Multi-rename tool. The keyboard shortcut (F2) is shown beside it.

@multiRename.presets.saved.description: Heading of the preset list at the top of the Presets menu: the user's presets, numbered 1–9 by position, including the ones Cmdr started the list with.

@multiRename.presets.reset.description: Presets menu item that sets every field back to its starting value, so all names stay as they are (Total Commander's <Default>).

@multiRename.presets.saveAs.description: Presets menu item that asks for a name and saves the tool's current settings as a new preset. The ellipsis means it asks for more before acting.

@multiRename.presets.rename.description: Item in a saved preset's submenu that asks for a new name for that preset.

@multiRename.presets.update.description: Item in a saved preset's submenu that overwrites that preset with the tool's current settings (every field). "settings" is the same noun as in commands.multiRenameSavePreset.label. Greyed out when the preset already matches them.

@multiRename.presets.moveUp.description: Item in a preset's submenu that moves that preset one place up the Presets list, so it swaps numbers (the 1–9 keys) with the one above. Greyed out on the top preset.

@multiRename.presets.moveDown.description: Item in a preset's submenu that moves that preset one place down the Presets list, so it swaps numbers (the 1–9 keys) with the one below. Greyed out on the bottom preset.

@multiRename.presets.delete.description: Item in a saved preset's submenu that deletes that preset. Only the preset goes; no files are touched.

@multiRename.presets.saveTitle.description: Accessible name of the small popup that asks for a name to save the current fields as a preset (opened with Cmd+S or Save as preset…).

@multiRename.presets.renameTitle.description: Accessible name of the small popup that asks for a new name for a saved preset.

@multiRename.presets.save.description: Button in the save-preset popup that saves the current fields under the typed name.

@multiRename.presets.renameConfirm.description: Button in the rename-preset popup that gives the preset the typed name. Renames the preset only, never files.

multiRename.presets.clash: There’s already a preset called “{preset}”. Replace it?

@multiRename.presets.clash.description: Shown in the preset-name popup when the typed name belongs to another saved preset. Pressing Enter again or the Replace button replaces that preset. {preset} is its name.

multiRename.presets.listFull: You have {max, number} presets, the most Cmdr keeps. Delete one to save this.

@multiRename.presets.listFull.description: Shown in the save-preset popup when the user tries to save a new preset but the list is already at its limit. Nothing was saved; the popup stays open. Deleting a preset (from its submenu in the Presets menu) makes room. {max} is the limit, 200.

@multiRename.presets.replace.description: Button in the preset-name popup, after the question whether to replace the preset that already has the name. Replaces that preset.

@multiRename.preset.dateAndTime.description: Name of a preset Cmdr starts the Presets list with, saved in this language the first time the list loads; the user can rename or delete it like their own. It names each file after its last-modified date and time, like 2026-07-14 09.05.30.

@multiRename.preset.removeDiacritics.description: Name of a preset Cmdr starts the Presets list with, saved in this language the first time the list loads; the user can rename or delete it like their own. It keeps names as they are but removes diacritics (á becomes a, ž becomes z). An everyday word for "accents" is fine. Keep this identical to multiRename.removeDiacritics, the option with the same effect.

@multiRename.preset.greekToLatin.description: Name of a preset Cmdr starts the Presets list with, saved in this language the first time the list loads; the user can rename or delete it like their own. It writes Greek letters in Latin ones (Αθήνα becomes Athina) and changes nothing else.

@multiRename.preset.normalizeUnicode.description: Name of a preset Cmdr starts the Presets list with, saved in this language the first time the list loads; the user can rename or delete it like their own. It only stores accented letters in the single-character form Windows, Linux, and websites expect; the names look the same.

@multiRename.presetName.description: Label of the name field in the small popup that saves the current fields as a preset (Cmd+S) or renames a saved one.

@multiRename.preview.description: Heading above the table that previews every file’s old and new name, styled like the field labels (“Name mask”, “Search for”), and the table’s accessible name. An error or a status line takes its place while one shows.

@multiRename.readingTags.description: Shown above the Multi-rename preview while Cmdr reads the photo, video, and music files' tags (date taken, artist, and so on) that the new names use. Counts files.

placeholders.readText: how many files were read, formatted
placeholders.totalText: how many photo, video, and music files there are, formatted

@multiRename.oldName.description: Preview table column: the file's current name.

@multiRename.newName.description: Preview table column: the name the file will get.

@multiRename.statusColumn.description: Header of the preview list's status column, read out by screen readers only: the column shows a small symbol on each row with a problem (invalid name, duplicate, name taken, gone), and nothing on rows that are ready or unchanged.

@multiRename.status.unchanged.description: Preview note: the new name is the same as the old one, so the file is left alone.

@multiRename.status.duplicate.description: Preview note: another file in this batch would get the same new name, so neither is renamed.

@multiRename.status.targetExists.description: Preview note: a file that stays in the folder already has this name.

@multiRename.status.invalidName.description: Preview note: the new name can't be a file name (empty, too long, or "." / "..").

@multiRename.status.disallowedCharacter.description: Preview note: the new name contains a character file names can't have, such as a slash. {character} is that character.

multiRename.error.unclosed: A placeholder is missing its closing “]”

@multiRename.error.unclosed.description: Shown when a mask has a [ without a matching ].

@multiRename.error.unknown.description: Shown when a mask has a placeholder that doesn't exist. {placeholder} is what's between the brackets.

@multiRename.error.badRegex.description: Shown when the search is a regular expression that can't be parsed.

multiRename.error.gone: This folder isn’t open any more. Close Multi-rename and open it again.

@multiRename.error.gone.description: Shown when the pane the tool renames in moved to another folder.

multiRename.error.nothingToRename: Nothing to rename: every new name is the same as the old one or has a problem

@multiRename.error.nothingToRename.description: Shown when Rename is pressed but no file is ready to be renamed.

multiRename.error.notConnected: This location isn’t connected right now

@multiRename.error.notConnected.description: Shown when the drive or server of the folder is no longer connected.

multiRename.error.couldntStart: Couldn’t start renaming. Try again in a moment.

@multiRename.error.couldntStart.description: Shown when the rename couldn't start (the rename queue refused it, or something went wrong inside Cmdr). Nothing was renamed.

multiRename.error.timedOut: That took too long, so Cmdr stopped waiting. Try again, or select fewer files.

@multiRename.error.timedOut.description: Shown under the Multi-rename preview when working out the new names, or getting the rename ready after Start, took longer than Cmdr waits. Nothing was renamed. 'Cmdr' is the app name; keep it untranslated.

multiRename.summary: {ready, plural, one {# to rename} other {# to rename}} · {unchanged, plural, one {# unchanged} other {# unchanged}} · <problemsToggle>{problems, plural, one {# problem} other {# problems}}</problemsToggle>

@multiRename.summary.description: Footer summary of the Multi-rename preview: how many files will be renamed, how many keep their name, and how many have a problem. While there are problems, the part inside <problemsToggle> is a link-styled toggle button: pressing it shows only the files with a problem in the preview list, pressing it again shows every file. Keep the <problemsToggle> tags around the problem count.

placeholders.ready: how many files get a new name
placeholders.unchanged: how many files keep their name
placeholders.problems: how many files can’t be renamed (invalid name, duplicate, name taken, gone)

multiRename.summaryReading: {ready, plural, one {# to rename} other {# to rename}} · {unchanged, plural, one {# unchanged} other {# unchanged}} · <problemsToggle>{problems, plural, one {# problem} other {# problems}}</problemsToggle> · {reading, plural, one {# still reading} other {# still reading}}

@multiRename.summaryReading.description: Footer summary of the Multi-rename preview while some files' tags are still being read: multiRename.summary plus how many files' new names wait for their tags. Keep the <problemsToggle> tags around the problem count, as in multiRename.summary.

placeholders.ready: how many files get a new name
placeholders.unchanged: how many files keep their name
placeholders.problems: how many files can’t be renamed
placeholders.reading: how many files' tags are still being read

@multiRename.cancel.description: Button that closes the tool without renaming.

@multiRename.undo.description: Footer button that reverses the last multi-rename of this session (all its files at once), right away, with no question first. It sits beside Cancel (multiRename.cancel), so the two must read differently. Shows its keyboard shortcut beside it.

multiRename.undoTooltip: {count, plural, one {Renames # file back to its old name} other {Renames # files back to their old names}}

@multiRename.undoTooltip.description: Tooltip of the Undo button: what pressing it will do. Keep it worded differently from multiRename.undoStarted, the toast saying the undo is underway. {count} is how many files the last multi-rename renamed.

multiRename.undoStarted: {count, plural, one {Renaming # file back} other {Renaming # files back}}.

@multiRename.undoStarted.description: Toast after Undo started reversing the last multi-rename: it says the undo is in progress. Keep it worded differently from multiRename.undoTooltip, which says what the button will do. {count} is how many files.

@multiRename.results.description: Footer button (Total Commander’s name for it) that opens the list of old and new names in the user’s text editor, so they can change any new name by hand. The trailing “…” is Cmdr’s mark for a command whose next step lets the user change what it does; keep it. Shows its keyboard shortcut beside it.

multiRename.results.editing: Edit the new names in your text editor and save the file. They show here when you come back to this window.

@multiRename.results.editing.description: Shown under the sheet’s fields while the names list is open in the text editor. Each line is an old name, a tab, and the new name.

@multiRename.movedRow.description: Screen-reader announcement (never shown) after the user moved the file under the cursor one place up or down in the Multi-rename preview list with Shift+Up or Shift+Down, which changes the order the files are renamed in (the order the counter numbers them). Say where the file now is, as a position in the list.

placeholders.positionText: the file's new position in the list, counting from 1, ready to drop into the sentence (for example 3)
placeholders.totalText: how many files the list holds, ready to drop into the sentence (for example 1,234)

multiRename.results.edited: {count, plural, one {# name comes from your edited list} other {# names come from your edited list}}.

@multiRename.results.edited.description: Shown under the sheet’s fields when the preview uses names the user typed in the text editor (Results). {count} is how many files carry such a name.

@multiRename.results.readNow.description: Link that reads the edited names list back right away, instead of waiting for the user to come back to the window.

@multiRename.results.discard.description: Link that drops the names typed in the text editor, so every file shows the name the settings give it.

multiRename.results.gone: The names list is gone. Open Results again to write a new one.

@multiRename.results.gone.description: Shown when the edited names list can’t be read back (it was deleted or moved).

multiRename.error.couldntWriteNames: Couldn’t write the names list. Check that your startup disk has free space.

@multiRename.error.couldntWriteNames.description: Shown when Results couldn’t create its text file in the temporary folder.

multiRename.resultsTooltip: Edit the new names in your text editor, then come back here to use them.

@multiRename.resultsTooltip.description: Tooltip of the Results… footer button (multiRename.results): it opens the list of old and new names in the user’s text editor, one file per line, to change any new name by hand; the sheet reads the list back when the user returns to the window. The tooltip shows the button’s keyboard shortcut after this text.

multiRename.editedName: You typed this name in Results

@multiRename.editedName.description: Tooltip and screen-reader text of a small pencil mark beside a row of the preview whose new name the user typed by hand in the list the Results… button opens (multiRename.results). “Results” here names that button: write it the way your multiRename.results label reads (without the “…”), quoted if your language quotes UI labels in running text rather than one the settings made.

@multiRename.history.description: A text field’s history: what it held when earlier renames ran. The accessible name of the chevron at the end of the name mask, extension mask, search, and replace fields (it opens the list), and of that list.

@multiRename.rename.description: Primary button that renames the files that are ready. {count} is how many.

@multiRename.starting.description: The Rename button's label while a rename waits for the files' tags to be read: it starts on its own once they are. Pressing the button again cancels the wait.

multiRename.renameWaitsTooltip: Some files’ tags are still being read. Rename waits for them, then starts.

@multiRename.renameWaitsTooltip.description: Tooltip on the Rename button while the name uses a photo, video, or music field (like the date taken) and Cmdr is still reading those from the files.

multiRename.startingTooltip: The rename starts once every file’s tags are read. Click again to cancel.

@multiRename.startingTooltip.description: Tooltip on the Rename button while it reads “Starting…” (multiRename.starting): the rename waits for the files' tags, and a second click cancels it.

multiRename.queuedAnnounce: Rename starts once the tags are read

@multiRename.queuedAnnounce.description: Spoken by screen readers when Rename was pressed while the files' tags are still being read: the rename waits and starts on its own.

@multiRename.queueCanceled.description: Spoken by screen readers when a rename that was waiting for the files' tags was canceled (Rename pressed again, or a field changed).

multiRename.started: {count, plural, one {Renaming # file} other {Renaming # files}}. You can roll it back from the operation log.

@multiRename.started.description: Toast after Rename starts. {count} is how many files. The operation log is the window listing past operations, where Undo is. "Roll back" is the button's name in the operation log (operationLog.dialog.rollBack): use the same words.

multiRename.error.previewOutOfDate: The folder changed since the preview. Check the new preview, then rename again.

@multiRename.error.previewOutOfDate.description: Shown when Rename is pressed but files in the folder changed after the preview was shown, so nothing was renamed and the preview is refreshed.

multiRename.error.readOnly: This folder can’t be renamed in: it’s inside an archive or another read-only place

@multiRename.error.readOnly.description: Shown when Rename is pressed in a folder that can't be changed, such as the inside of a zip archive.

@multiRename.status.missing.description: Preview note: an item (file or folder) the user picked for renaming was deleted or moved out of the folder while the tool was open, so it can't be renamed.

@multiRename.status.ready.description: Screen-reader text in the preview's status column for an item (file or folder) that will be renamed. Restructure freely to avoid agreeing with a gendered noun (for example "Will be renamed"). Sighted users see no mark on these rows; only the problem rows get a symbol.

multiRename.reason.duplicate: Another file in this batch gets the same new name, so neither is renamed.

@multiRename.reason.duplicate.description: Tooltip on the preview's duplicate symbol: the full reason behind multiRename.status.duplicate. The row can be a file or a folder: where your language’s word for “file” excludes folders, use a neutral word for the item, or restructure.

multiRename.reason.targetExists: A file that stays in this folder already has this name, so this one keeps its name.

@multiRename.reason.targetExists.description: Tooltip on the preview's "name is taken" symbol: the full reason behind multiRename.status.targetExists. The file that holds the name isn't part of the rename (or can't be renamed itself). The row can be a file or a folder: where your language’s word for “file” excludes folders, use a neutral word for the item, or restructure.

multiRename.reason.missing: This file was moved or deleted after Multi-rename opened, so it’s left out.

@multiRename.reason.missing.description: Tooltip on the preview's "gone" symbol: the full reason behind multiRename.status.missing. "Multi-rename" is the tool's name; match multiRename.title. The row can be a file or a folder: where your language’s word for “file” excludes folders, use a neutral word for the item, or restructure.

@multiRename.status.reading.description: Quiet preview note on a row whose photo, video, or music file is still being read for its date taken or tags, so its new name may still change. Not a problem; it clears by itself.

@multiRename.status.noValue.description: Short preview note: the file has no value for a field the name mask uses, so it can't be renamed. {field} is the field's name, like “Date taken” or “Artist” (multiRename.mediaField.*), and its grammatical gender varies: if “missing” would have to agree with it, a form like “{field}: no value” is fine.

placeholders.field: the field's name, like Date taken or Artist

multiRename.reason.noValue: This file has no “{field}” value, so it keeps its name.

@multiRename.reason.noValue.description: Tooltip on the preview's "field missing" symbol: the full reason behind multiRename.status.noValue. A field is a piece of the file's own information, like the date a photo was taken or a song's artist. The row can be a file or a folder: where your language’s word for “file” excludes folders, use a neutral word for the item, or restructure.

placeholders.field: the field's name, like Artist or Camera

multiRename.reason.noDate: This file has no “{field}” value, so it keeps its name. The placeholder’s editor can use the date the file was last changed instead.

@multiRename.reason.noDate.description: Tooltip on the preview's "field missing" symbol for a date field (like the date a photo was taken). The placeholder's editor opens from the placeholder in the name mask; it has a choice to fall back to the file's last-changed date. The row can be a file or a folder: where your language’s word for “file” excludes folders, use a neutral word for the item, or restructure.

placeholders.field: the date field's name, like Date taken

@multiRename.status.unreadable.description: Short preview note: Cmdr couldn't read the file's tags or photo information (EXIF), which a field in the name mask needs, so it can't be renamed.

multiRename.reason.unreadable: Multi-rename couldn’t read this file’s tags or photo information, so it has no “{field}” value and keeps its name.

@multiRename.reason.unreadable.description: Tooltip on the preview's "can't read tags" symbol: the full reason behind multiRename.status.unreadable. "Multi-rename" is the tool's name; match multiRename.title. Tags are a music or video file's artist, title, and so on; photo information is a photo's date taken, camera, and so on. The row can be a file or a folder: where your language’s word for “file” excludes folders, use a neutral word for the item, or restructure.

placeholders.field: the field's name, like Date taken or Artist

@multiRename.mediaField.exifTaken.description: Name of a field Multi-rename can put in a file name: the date and time a photo or video was taken, from its EXIF or video metadata. Shown in the field picker, in reasons (“This file has no “Date taken” value”), and in the field's editor.

@multiRename.mediaField.exifCamera.description: Name of a photo field Multi-rename can put in a file name: the camera's maker and model together, like “Apple iPhone 15 Pro”.

@multiRename.mediaField.exifMake.description: Name of a photo field Multi-rename can put in a file name: the company that made the camera, like “Canon”.

@multiRename.mediaField.exifModel.description: Name of a photo field Multi-rename can put in a file name: the camera's model, like “EOS R6”.

@multiRename.mediaField.exifLens.description: Name of a photo field Multi-rename can put in a file name: the lens the photo was taken with.

@multiRename.mediaField.exifIso.description: Name of a photo field Multi-rename can put in a file name: the ISO speed (light sensitivity) setting, a number like 400. Keep “ISO” as is in most languages.

@multiRename.mediaField.exifFocal.description: Name of a photo field Multi-rename can put in a file name: the lens's focal length in whole millimeters, like 24.

@multiRename.mediaField.exifWidth.description: Name of a photo field Multi-rename can put in a file name: the image's width in pixels.

@multiRename.mediaField.exifHeight.description: Name of a photo field Multi-rename can put in a file name: the image's height in pixels.

@multiRename.mediaField.exifOrientation.description: Name of a photo field Multi-rename can put in a file name: the EXIF orientation, a number from 1 to 8 saying how the photo is rotated.

@multiRename.mediaField.tagTitle.description: Name of a music field Multi-rename can put in a file name: the song's title, from the file's tags.

@multiRename.mediaField.tagArtist.description: Name of a music field Multi-rename can put in a file name: the song's artist, from the file's tags.

@multiRename.mediaField.tagAlbumArtist.description: Name of a music field Multi-rename can put in a file name: the album's artist (which can differ from a song's own artist on a compilation).

@multiRename.mediaField.tagAlbum.description: Name of a music field Multi-rename can put in a file name: the album's name.

@multiRename.mediaField.tagTrack.description: Name of a music field Multi-rename can put in a file name: the song's number on its album.

@multiRename.mediaField.tagDisc.description: Name of a music field Multi-rename can put in a file name: which disc of a multi-disc album the song is on.

@multiRename.mediaField.tagYear.description: Name of a music field Multi-rename can put in a file name: the year the song or album came out.

@multiRename.mediaField.tagGenre.description: Name of a music field Multi-rename can put in a file name: the song's genre, like “Electronic”.

@multiRename.mediaField.tagComment.description: Name of a music field Multi-rename can put in a file name: the free-text comment in the file's tags.

multiRename.mediaPicker.title: Insert a field

@multiRename.mediaPicker.title.description: Accessible name of the Multi-rename field picker, a small popup listing the photo, video, and music fields (date taken, camera, artist, title, …) that can go into the new name. Also the accessible name of the button that opens it.

@multiRename.mediaPicker.filter.description: Placeholder and accessible name of the field picker's filter box: typing narrows the list of fields.

@multiRename.mediaPicker.photos.description: Heading of the field picker's group of photo and video fields. Keep “EXIF” as is: it's the name of the photo metadata format, and people search for it.

@multiRename.mediaPicker.music.description: Heading of the field picker's group of music fields. Keep “ID3”, “MP4”, and “FLAC” as is: they're the tag formats' names, and people search for them.

@multiRename.mediaPicker.none.description: Dimmed note in the field picker, where a field's example value would be: none of the files being renamed has this field. Lowercase: it sits beside the field's name like a value.

@multiRename.mediaPicker.noneYet.description: Dimmed note in the field picker, where a field's example value would be: none of the files read so far has this field, while Cmdr is still reading the rest. Lowercase: it sits beside the field's name like a value.

@multiRename.mediaPicker.noMatch.description: Shown in the field picker when the text typed in its filter box matches no field.

placeholders.filter: what the user typed in the filter box

@multiRename.mediaPicker.inserted.description: Spoken by screen readers after the field picker put a field into the name mask. The picker stays open for more.

placeholders.field: the field's name, like Date taken

@multiRename.mediaPicker.insertedMark.description: Screen-reader text after a field's name in the field picker, for a field already put into the name mask while the picker was open (shown as a check mark). Lowercase: read right after the name. The field names vary in grammatical gender, so if “inserted” would have to agree with one, a neutral form like “already in the mask” is fine.

@multiRename.mediaEditor.marker.description: Accessible name of the small ▾ marker under a photo, video, or music field placeholder (like [=exif.taken:d]) in the Multi-rename name mask: it opens the field's editor.

multiRename.mediaEditor.title: Field

@multiRename.mediaEditor.title.description: Accessible name of the small popup that edits a photo, video, or music field placeholder (like [=exif.taken:d]) in the Multi-rename name mask: its format, and for a date, what to use when a file has none.

@multiRename.mediaEditor.format.description: Label of the field editor's text box for a date field's format, written in date letters (like Y-M-D or YMD_hms).

multiRename.mediaEditor.dateHint: Y, M, and D for the date, h, m, and s for the time, with - . _ or spaces between. Leave empty for the date and time.

@multiRename.mediaEditor.dateHint.description: Hint under the field editor's date format box. Keep the letters Y, M, D, h, m, s and the characters - . _ as they are: they're the format's syntax.

@multiRename.mediaEditor.presets.description: Accessible name of the row of format buttons in a date field's editor (Date and time, Date, Time, Compact).

@multiRename.mediaEditor.preset.dateTime.description: A format button in a date field's editor: the whole date and time, like 2026-07-14 09.05.30.

@multiRename.mediaEditor.preset.date.description: A format button in a date field's editor: the date alone, like 2026-07-14.

@multiRename.mediaEditor.preset.time.description: A format button in a date field's editor: the time alone, like 09.05.30.

@multiRename.mediaEditor.preset.compact.description: A format button in a date field's editor: the date and time with no separators but one underscore, like 20260714_090530. It names a date FORMAT (the noun it agrees with), not the UI density option settings.appearance.uiDensity.opt.compact, which shares the English word.

@multiRename.mediaEditor.digits.description: Label of the field editor's box for a number field (like a track number): how many digits, padded with leading zeros.

multiRename.mediaEditor.digitsHint: Pads with leading zeros, so 2 turns 3 into 03. Leave empty for the number as it is.

@multiRename.mediaEditor.digitsHint.description: Hint under the field editor's Digits box for a number field that doesn't pad by itself (like ISO): empty shows the number as it is.

multiRename.mediaEditor.digitsHintTrack: Pads with leading zeros, so 2 turns 3 into 03. Leave empty to pad to the longest number in these files, like 07 for 42 tracks.

@multiRename.mediaEditor.digitsHintTrack.description: Hint under the field editor's Digits box for the track and disc number fields, which pad by themselves when it is empty.

multiRename.mediaEditor.digitsInvalid: Type how many digits, like 2, or zeros, like 00.

@multiRename.mediaEditor.digitsInvalid.description: Shown under the field editor's Digits box while what was typed can't be read as a digit count (like 0 or letters).

@multiRename.mediaEditor.characters.description: Label of the field editor's box for a text field (like an artist): which characters to take, written as a range like 1-10.

multiRename.mediaEditor.charactersHint: Like 1-10 for the first ten, or -3- for the last three. Leave empty for all of it.

@multiRename.mediaEditor.charactersHint.description: Hint under the field editor's Characters box for a text field. Keep 1-10 and -3- as they are: they're the range syntax.

multiRename.mediaEditor.fallback: When a file has none: use the date it was last changed

@multiRename.mediaEditor.fallback.description: Checkbox in a date field's editor (like the date a photo was taken): a file without that date gets the date it was last changed instead, so it can still be renamed.

multiRename.mediaEditor.usesModified: {count, plural, one {{countText} file uses the date it was last changed} other {{countText} files use the date they were last changed}}

@multiRename.mediaEditor.usesModified.description: Under the fallback checkbox in a date field's editor, while it's on: how many of the files have no such date and take the date they were last changed instead.

placeholders.count: how many files, for the plural
placeholders.countText: the same number, formatted

multiRename.mediaEditor.missing: {count, plural, one {{countText} file has none and keeps its name} other {{countText} files have none and keep their names}}

@multiRename.mediaEditor.missing.description: In a field's editor: how many of the files lack this field, so they won't be renamed.

placeholders.count: how many files, for the plural
placeholders.countText: the same number, formatted

multiRename.mediaEditor.stillReading: {count, plural, one {{countText} file is still being read} other {{countText} files are still being read}}

@multiRename.mediaEditor.stillReading.description: In a field's editor: how many of the files Cmdr is still reading this information from.

placeholders.count: how many files, for the plural
placeholders.countText: the same number, formatted

@multiRename.mediaEditor.gap.reading.description: In a field's editor's list of example files: this file is still being read. Lowercase: it stands where the field's value would.

@multiRename.mediaEditor.gap.noValue.description: In a field's editor's list of example files: this file doesn't have the field. Lowercase: it stands where the field's value would.

@multiRename.mediaEditor.gap.unreadable.description: In a field's editor's list of example files: Cmdr couldn't read this file's tags or photo information. Lowercase: it stands where the field's value would.

@multiRename.reason.empty.description: Tooltip on the preview's "not a valid name" symbol when the masks produce an empty name.

multiRename.reason.tooLong: The new name is too long for a file name.

@multiRename.reason.tooLong.description: Tooltip on the preview's "not a valid name" symbol when the new name is longer than a file name may be.

@multiRename.reason.reserved.description: Tooltip on the preview's "not a valid name" symbol when the new name is "." or "..", which name a folder itself and its parent. Keep both dot names exactly as they are.

@multiRename.reason.disallowedCharacter.description: Tooltip on the preview's "not a valid name" symbol when the new name holds a character file names can't have, such as a slash. {character} is that character.

multiRename.selectionChanged: The folder changed while Multi-rename was opening. Check your selection, then try again.

@multiRename.selectionChanged.description: Warning toast when ⌃M (Multi-rename) didn't open because files appeared or disappeared in the folder at that moment, so the selected rows may no longer be the files the user picked. Nothing was renamed.

multiRename.swapsSkipped: {count, plural, one {Skipped # rename that swaps names} other {Skipped # renames that swap names}}. Rename them one at a time.

@multiRename.swapsSkipped.description: Warning toast after Rename starts on cloud storage (S3), when some renames swap names with each other (for example a → b and b → a). On S3, renaming a folder copies everything inside it, and copying one folder onto another that is still there would mix their contents, so those renames were skipped and the files kept their names. {count} is how many (always 2 or more). Match the wording of askCmdr.renameUndo.swapsSkipped.

@multiRename.archiveTitle.description: Alert title when ⌃M (Multi-rename) is pressed while browsing inside a zip archive. Cmdr can rename files in a zip one by one, but the Multi-rename tool only works in folders on a drive. "Multi-rename" is the tool’s name; match multiRename.title.

multiRename.archiveMessage: To rename files in this zip, rename them one at a time.

@multiRename.archiveMessage.description: Alert body under multiRename.archiveTitle. Points the user to renaming files inside the zip one by one (the regular single-file rename), which does work there.

@multiRename.counterEditor.marker.description: Accessible name (read by screen readers) of the small ▾ button drawn right after each counter placeholder [C] in the Multi-rename mask field. Clicking it opens a popover that edits one counter placeholder ([C], or [C10+5:3] with its own start, step, and digits) in the Multi-rename name or extension mask. It opens from a small ▾ after the placeholder, or with the down arrow key while the text cursor is in it. A VERB phrase.

multiRename.counterEditor.title: Counter

@multiRename.counterEditor.title.description: Accessible name of the small popover that edits one counter placeholder ([C], or [C10+5:3] with its own start, step, and digits) in the Multi-rename name or extension mask. It opens from a small ▾ after the placeholder, or with the down arrow key while the text cursor is in it. A NOUN: the counter that numbers the renamed files.

@multiRename.counterEditor.start.description: Label of the number field in the small popover that edits one counter placeholder ([C], or [C10+5:3] with its own start, step, and digits) in the Multi-rename name or extension mask. It opens from a small ▾ after the placeholder, or with the down arrow key while the text cursor is in it: the number the first file gets. A NOUN (where counting starts), not a verb.

@multiRename.counterEditor.step.description: Label of the number field in the small popover that edits one counter placeholder ([C], or [C10+5:3] with its own start, step, and digits) in the Multi-rename name or extension mask. It opens from a small ▾ after the placeholder, or with the down arrow key while the text cursor is in it: how much the number goes up per file (down, when negative). A NOUN.

@multiRename.counterEditor.digits.description: Label of the number field in the small popover that edits one counter placeholder ([C], or [C10+5:3] with its own start, step, and digits) in the Multi-rename name or extension mask. It opens from a small ▾ after the placeholder, or with the down arrow key while the text cursor is in it: how many digits the number has at least; shorter numbers get leading zeros (3 digits turns 7 into 007). A NOUN.

@multiRename.counterEditor.counts.description: Plain-language line under the fields of the small popover that edits one counter placeholder ([C], or [C10+5:3] with its own start, step, and digits) in the Multi-rename name or extension mask. It opens from a small ▾ under the placeholder, when the text cursor rests in it, or when the mouse rests on it. Shows the first three numbers the counter gives, exactly as they appear in the new names (with leading zeros when the counter has more digits).

placeholders.first: the first file’s number as it appears in the name (e.g. 1, or 001)
placeholders.second: the second file’s number as it appears in the name (e.g. 3, or 003)
placeholders.third: the third file’s number as it appears in the name (e.g. 5, or 005)

multiRename.placeholderHelp.name: The file’s name, without its extension

@multiRename.placeholderHelp.name.description: In the Multi-rename sheet, a tooltip on a placeholder button (such as [N], [E], or [C]) explains what that placeholder puts in the new name, lists a few of its other forms, and shows each with an example on a made-up file (Beach day.jpg, in the folder Trips/Lisbon 2026, last changed 2026-07-14 09:05:30). What the [N] placeholder stands for. A noun phrase.

@multiRename.placeholderHelp.extension.description: In the Multi-rename sheet, a tooltip on a placeholder button (such as [N], [E], or [C]) explains what that placeholder puts in the new name, lists a few of its other forms, and shows each with an example on a made-up file (Beach day.jpg, in the folder Trips/Lisbon 2026, last changed 2026-07-14 09:05:30). What the [E] placeholder stands for, for example “pdf”. A noun phrase.

multiRename.placeholderHelp.parent: The name of the folder the file is in

@multiRename.placeholderHelp.parent.description: In the Multi-rename sheet, a tooltip on a placeholder button (such as [N], [E], or [C]) explains what that placeholder puts in the new name, lists a few of its other forms, and shows each with an example on a made-up file (Beach day.jpg, in the folder Trips/Lisbon 2026, last changed 2026-07-14 09:05:30). What the [P] placeholder stands for. A noun phrase.

multiRename.placeholderHelp.counter: A number that goes up by one step per file, in the list’s order

@multiRename.placeholderHelp.counter.description: In the Multi-rename sheet, a tooltip on a placeholder button (such as [N], [E], or [C]) explains what that placeholder puts in the new name, lists a few of its other forms, and shows each with an example on a made-up file (Beach day.jpg, in the folder Trips/Lisbon 2026, last changed 2026-07-14 09:05:30). What the [C] counter placeholder stands for. A noun phrase.

multiRename.placeholderHelp.date: The date the file was last changed: year, month, and day

@multiRename.placeholderHelp.date.description: In the Multi-rename sheet, a tooltip on a placeholder button (such as [N], [E], or [C]) explains what that placeholder puts in the new name, lists a few of its other forms, and shows each with an example on a made-up file (Beach day.jpg, in the folder Trips/Lisbon 2026, last changed 2026-07-14 09:05:30). What the [YMD] placeholder stands for (the modification date, as 20261009). A noun phrase.

multiRename.placeholderHelp.time: The time the file was last changed: hours, minutes, and seconds

@multiRename.placeholderHelp.time.description: In the Multi-rename sheet, a tooltip on a placeholder button (such as [N], [E], or [C]) explains what that placeholder puts in the new name, lists a few of its other forms, and shows each with an example on a made-up file (Beach day.jpg, in the folder Trips/Lisbon 2026, last changed 2026-07-14 09:05:30). What the [hms] placeholder stands for (the modification time, as 143207). A noun phrase.

multiRename.placeholderHelp.media: A photo’s, video’s, or song’s own information: EXIF, ID3, MP4, FLAC, Ogg, and more

@multiRename.placeholderHelp.media.description: Head line of the tooltip on the Multi-rename “media ▾” button (multiRename.mediaButton), after the placeholder form [=…]: these placeholders put information stored inside the file (a photo's date taken and camera, a song's artist and title) into the new name. Keep the format names EXIF, ID3, MP4, FLAC, and Ogg as is: people search for them.

multiRename.placeholderHelp.mediaTaken: The date a photo or video was taken

@multiRename.placeholderHelp.mediaTaken.description: In the “media ▾” button's tooltip, beside the form [=exif.taken:d]: what it puts in the name. An example follows.

multiRename.placeholderHelp.mediaFallbac: With the date the file was last changed for one without it

@multiRename.placeholderHelp.mediaFallba.description: In the “media ▾” button's tooltip, beside the form [=exif.taken|modified:YMD_hms]: the date taken, and for a file that has none, the date it was last changed instead. An example follows.

@multiRename.placeholderHelp.mediaCamera.description: In the “media ▾” button's tooltip, beside the form [=exif.camera]: what it puts in the name, like “Apple iPhone 15 Pro”. An example follows.

multiRename.placeholderHelp.mediaSong: A song’s track number, artist, and title

@multiRename.placeholderHelp.mediaSong.description: In the “media ▾” button's tooltip, beside the mask [=tag.track:2] [=tag.artist] - [=tag.title]: what it puts in the name, like “03 Daft Punk - Digital Love”. An example follows.

multiRename.placeholderHelp.mediaHint: Click to pick from every field, each with its value on your files.

@multiRename.placeholderHelp.mediaHint.description: Last line of the “media ▾” button's tooltip: clicking the button opens a list of every photo, video, and music field, each showing what it holds in the files being renamed.

@multiRename.placeholderHelp.oneChar.description: In the Multi-rename sheet, a tooltip on a placeholder button (such as [N], [E], or [C]) explains what that placeholder puts in the new name, lists a few of its other forms, and shows each with an example on a made-up file (Beach day.jpg, in the folder Trips/Lisbon 2026, last changed 2026-07-14 09:05:30). Meaning of a form like [N3]: only that one character of the name. Positions count from 1.

@multiRename.placeholderHelp.charRange.description: In the Multi-rename sheet, a tooltip on a placeholder button (such as [N], [E], or [C]) explains what that placeholder puts in the new name, lists a few of its other forms, and shows each with an example on a made-up file (Beach day.jpg, in the folder Trips/Lisbon 2026, last changed 2026-07-14 09:05:30). Meaning of a form like [N2-5]: that run of characters, both ends included. Positions count from 1.

multiRename.placeholderHelp.allButLast: {count, plural, one {All but the last character} other {All but the last # characters}}

@multiRename.placeholderHelp.allButLast.description: In the Multi-rename sheet, a tooltip on a placeholder button (such as [N], [E], or [C]) explains what that placeholder puts in the new name, lists a few of its other forms, and shows each with an example on a made-up file (Beach day.jpg, in the folder Trips/Lisbon 2026, last changed 2026-07-14 09:05:30). Meaning of a form like [N1--2]: from the first character up to the second-to-last one, so the name without its last few characters (Beach day becomes Beach da).

placeholders.count: how many characters at the end are left out (e.g. 1)

multiRename.placeholderHelp.charsFrom: {count, plural, one {# character} other {# characters}}, starting at character {from}

@multiRename.placeholderHelp.charsFrom.description: In the Multi-rename sheet, a tooltip on a placeholder button (such as [N], [E], or [C]) explains what that placeholder puts in the new name, lists a few of its other forms, and shows each with an example on a made-up file (Beach day.jpg, in the folder Trips/Lisbon 2026, last changed 2026-07-14 09:05:30). placeholders.from: the position of the first one, counted from 1 (e.g. 7)

multiRename.placeholderHelp.lastChars: {count, plural, one {The last character} other {The last # characters}}

@multiRename.placeholderHelp.lastChars.description: In the Multi-rename sheet, a tooltip on a placeholder button (such as [N], [E], or [C]) explains what that placeholder puts in the new name, lists a few of its other forms, and shows each with an example on a made-up file (Beach day.jpg, in the folder Trips/Lisbon 2026, last changed 2026-07-14 09:05:30). Meaning of a form like [N-3,3]: the last few characters, counted from the end.

placeholders.count: how many characters from the end (e.g. 3)

@multiRename.placeholderHelp.firstChar.description: In the Multi-rename sheet, a tooltip on a placeholder button (such as [N], [E], or [C]) explains what that placeholder puts in the new name, lists a few of its other forms, and shows each with an example on a made-up file (Beach day.jpg, in the folder Trips/Lisbon 2026, last changed 2026-07-14 09:05:30). Meaning of a form like [E1]: only the first character.

multiRename.placeholderHelp.firstChars: {count, plural, one {The first character} other {The first # characters}}

@multiRename.placeholderHelp.firstChars.description: In the Multi-rename sheet, a tooltip on a placeholder button (such as [N], [E], or [C]) explains what that placeholder puts in the new name, lists a few of its other forms, and shows each with an example on a made-up file (Beach day.jpg, in the folder Trips/Lisbon 2026, last changed 2026-07-14 09:05:30). placeholders.count: how many characters from the start (e.g. 3)

multiRename.placeholderHelp.grandparent: The name of the folder above the file’s folder

@multiRename.placeholderHelp.grandparent.description: In the Multi-rename sheet, a tooltip on a placeholder button (such as [N], [E], or [C]) explains what that placeholder puts in the new name, lists a few of its other forms, and shows each with an example on a made-up file (Beach day.jpg, in the folder Trips/Lisbon 2026, last changed 2026-07-14 09:05:30). Meaning of [G]: the folder that holds the file’s folder (the grandparent folder). A noun phrase.

@multiRename.placeholderHelp.counterStar.description: In the Multi-rename sheet, a tooltip on a placeholder button (such as [N], [E], or [C]) explains what that placeholder puts in the new name, lists a few of its other forms, and shows each with an example on a made-up file (Beach day.jpg, in the folder Trips/Lisbon 2026, last changed 2026-07-14 09:05:30). Meaning of a counter form like [C10]: the first file gets this number.

@multiRename.placeholderHelp.counterStep.description: In the Multi-rename sheet, a tooltip on a placeholder button (such as [N], [E], or [C]) explains what that placeholder puts in the new name, lists a few of its other forms, and shows each with an example on a made-up file (Beach day.jpg, in the folder Trips/Lisbon 2026, last changed 2026-07-14 09:05:30). Meaning of a counter form like [C+5]: how much the number grows per file.

placeholders.step: how much the number grows per file (e.g. 5)

multiRename.placeholderHelp.counterDigit: {digits, plural, one {At least # digit} other {At least # digits}}, with leading zeros

@multiRename.placeholderHelp.counterDigi.description: In the Multi-rename sheet, a tooltip on a placeholder button (such as [N], [E], or [C]) explains what that placeholder puts in the new name, lists a few of its other forms, and shows each with an example on a made-up file (Beach day.jpg, in the folder Trips/Lisbon 2026, last changed 2026-07-14 09:05:30). multiRename.placeholderHelp.counterAll: All three at once; a minus step counts down

@multiRename.placeholderHelp.counterAll.description: In the Multi-rename sheet, a tooltip on a placeholder button (such as [N], [E], or [C]) explains what that placeholder puts in the new name, lists a few of its other forms, and shows each with an example on a made-up file (Beach day.jpg, in the folder Trips/Lisbon 2026, last changed 2026-07-14 09:05:30). Meaning of a counter form like [C10-1:2] that sets the start, the step, and the digits together; a step with a minus sign makes the numbers go down.

@multiRename.placeholderHelp.isoDate.description: In the Multi-rename sheet, a tooltip on a placeholder button (such as [N], [E], or [C]) explains what that placeholder puts in the new name, lists a few of its other forms, and shows each with an example on a made-up file (Beach day.jpg, in the folder Trips/Lisbon 2026, last changed 2026-07-14 09:05:30). multiRename.placeholderHelp.dateSeparato: Any parts, with dashes, dots, underscores, or spaces between them

@multiRename.placeholderHelp.dottedTime.description: In the Multi-rename sheet, a tooltip on a placeholder button (such as [N], [E], or [C]) explains what that placeholder puts in the new name, lists a few of its other forms, and shows each with an example on a made-up file (Beach day.jpg, in the folder Trips/Lisbon 2026, last changed 2026-07-14 09:05:30).
