multiRename.tags.wouldDrop.message: {count, plural, one {Writing {countText} file would drop the tag data listed below, which the editor doesn’t show. It wasn’t written.} other {Writing {countText} files would drop the tag data listed below, which the editor doesn’t show. They weren’t written.}}

@multiRename.tags.wouldDrop.message.description: Shown in the tag editor window: under the would-lose-data heading. The list below names each file and the tag items it would lose.

placeholders.countText: how many files, ready to drop into the sentence (for example 1,234)

multiRename.tags.wouldDrop.listLabel: Files that would lose tag data

@multiRename.tags.wouldDrop.listLabel.description: Shown in the tag editor window: the accessible name of the list of files that would lose tag data.

@multiRename.tags.wouldDrop.row.description: Shown in the tag editor window: one file that would lose tag data, and the items (technical tag IDs such as TSOP or COMM:ces, do not translate them).

placeholders.items: technical tag IDs, like TSOP, TXXX:Comment

@multiRename.tags.wouldDrop.writeAnyway.description: Shown in the tag editor window: writes the files that would lose tag data anyway, dropping the listed items.

@multiRename.tags.wouldDrop.skip.description: Shown in the tag editor window: leaves the files that would lose tag data unwritten.

multiRename.tags.write.summaryAs: {count, plural, one {Writing as {kind}: {countText} file will change:} other {Writing as {kind}: {countText} files will change:}}

@multiRename.tags.write.summaryAs.description: Shown in the tag editor window: heading of the list of files a write will change, before anything is written. It names the chosen content kind.

placeholders.kind: the content kind the tags are written as: Audiobook or Music
placeholders.countText: how many files, ready to drop into the sentence (for example 1,234)

@multiRename.tags.write.refused.description: Shown in the tag editor window: after a write that wrote no file at all (refused before touching any file, or every file was left unwritten). A reason follows.

@multiRename.tags.write.waiting.description: Shown in the tag editor window, beside a spinner, after the user pressed Write: the app waits for the last tag edit to land before it lists or writes the changes.

multiRename.tags.write.stillBusy: Cmdr is still reading the files. Try again in a moment.

@multiRename.tags.write.stillBusy.description: Shown in the tag editor window, next to the Write buttons: the app waited for an earlier tag call to finish and gave up, so nothing was listed or written. The user can press again.

multiRename.tags.write.listFailed: Cmdr couldn’t check what will change. Try again in a moment.

@multiRename.tags.write.listFailed.description: Shown in the tag editor window, next to the Write buttons: the list of what a write will change couldn’t be made, so nothing was written.

multiRename.tags.write.sessionGone: The tags aren’t open any more. Close Multi-Rename and open it again.

@multiRename.tags.write.sessionGone.description: Shown in the tag editor window after “No file was written.”: the app’s session for these files ended, so the write was refused.

multiRename.tags.write.stopped: The write stopped before it finished, so some files may not have their new tags.

@multiRename.tags.write.stopped.description: Shown in the tag editor window: a write ended unexpectedly, possibly after writing some files.

multiRename.tags.write.noUndoSome: Some of these files can’t be undone: their old tags couldn’t be kept. Undo tag changes restores the others.

@multiRename.tags.write.noUndoSome.description: Shown in the tag editor window: after a write where only some files’ old tags could be kept for Undo.

multiRename.tags.undoStoreUnavailable: Couldn’t use the store that keeps the old tags for Undo.

@multiRename.tags.undoStoreUnavailable.description: Shown in the tag editor window: when a write or an undo couldn’t go on because the app couldn’t save or read the old tags.

multiRename.tags.undo.unwrittenLost: Tag changes you haven’t written to those files yet are lost too.

@multiRename.tags.undo.unwrittenLost.description: Second sentence of the question asked in the tag editor window before undoing the last tag write, when some tag changes are not written yet.

@multiRename.tags.select.all.description: Accessible name of the checkbox in the header of the tracks pane of the tag editor window. It selects or deselects every track; the tag tools then work on the selected tracks only (all tracks when none is selected). Only read aloud by screen readers.

@multiRename.tags.choices.button.description: Small button at the end of a «multiple values» row of the shared tags table in the tag editor window. It opens a list of the distinct values the files hold, to pick one for every file.

multiRename.tags.choices.label: {field} values

@multiRename.tags.choices.label.description: Accessible name of the Values button of a row in the tag editor window, and of the list it opens. Only read aloud by screen readers.

placeholders.field: the name of the tag the row edits, like Album or Genre

@multiRename.tags.choices.item.description: One entry in the list of values of a «multiple values» row in the tag editor window: a value the files hold and, in brackets, how many files have exactly it. Picking it sets it on every file.

placeholders.value: the tag value, like an album title; several values of a multi-value tag are already joined with semicolons
placeholders.countText: how many files have exactly this value, ready to drop into the text (for example 1,234)

@multiRename.tags.choices.empty.description: Greyed text for a value in the list of a «multiple values» row in the tag editor window when some files have no value for that tag at all.

multiRename.tags.selectionGone: The selected tracks are no longer here, so nothing was changed. Select tracks again, or run the tool with none selected for all tracks.

@multiRename.tags.selectionGone.description: Notice in the tag editor window: the user selected some tracks in the tracks pane, then they disappeared (for example renamed elsewhere), and a tag tool was pressed. The tool did not run, so it can’t change every track by surprise.

@multiRename.tags.tools.replace.button.description: Button in the tag editor window that opens the panel for replacing text inside tag values (not in file names).

@multiRename.tags.tools.format.button.description: Button in the tag editor window that opens the panel which rebuilds one tag from a Multi-rename mask such as [N3-].

@multiRename.tags.tools.replace.fieldsLa.description: Accessible name of the group of checkboxes choosing which tag fields the Find and replace panel changes in the tag editor window.

@multiRename.tags.tools.replace.allField.description: Checkbox in the Find and replace panel of the tag editor window: change every tag field instead of the checked ones.

@multiRename.tags.tools.replace.search.description: Label of the text box with the text to find in the Find and replace panel of the tag editor window.

@multiRename.tags.tools.replace.replaceW.description: Label of the text box with the replacement text in the Find and replace panel of the tag editor window.

@multiRename.tags.tools.replace.run.description: Button that runs Find and replace on the tag values of the files in the tag editor window. Disabled while the Find box is empty.

@multiRename.tags.tools.format.field.description: Label of the tag field picker in the Format a field panel of the tag editor window.

@multiRename.tags.tools.format.mask.description: Label of the mask text box in the Format a field panel of the tag editor window. The mask is a Multi-rename mask where [N] stands for the field’s current value.

multiRename.tags.tools.format.hint: Format keeps only the first value of a field that holds several, such as Artist or Genre.

@multiRename.tags.tools.format.hint.description: Hint under the Format a field panel in the tag editor window: a field with several values (Artist, Genre) ends with just one value, built from the first.

@multiRename.tags.tools.format.run.description: Button that rebuilds the chosen tag field from the mask in the tag editor window.

multiRename.tags.tools.name.mode: How to read the file names

@multiRename.tags.tools.name.mode.description: Accessible name of the switch between a simple pattern and a regular expression in the From file name panel of the tag editor window.

@multiRename.tags.tools.name.modePattern.description: Option in the From file name panel of the tag editor window: read file names with a simple pattern such as %track% - %title%.

@multiRename.tags.tools.name.modeRegex.description: Option in the From file name panel of the tag editor window: read file names with a regular expression whose named groups are tag fields.

@multiRename.tags.tools.name.patternPatt.description: Label of the pattern text box in the From file name panel of the tag editor window while the Pattern mode is on. The percent signs wrap tag field names and must stay as they are.

@multiRename.tags.tools.name.patternRege.description: Label of the pattern text box in the From file name panel of the tag editor window while the Regular expression mode is on. Named groups are tag field names.

placeholders.example: a sample regular expression with named groups, like (?<track>\d+)_(?<title>.+); never translate it

@multiRename.tags.tools.name.recent.description: Accessible name of the list of the patterns used last in the From file name panel of the tag editor window. Picking one fills the pattern box.

@multiRename.tags.tools.name.preview.description: Button in the From file name panel of the tag editor window: shows what the pattern reads from each file name without changing any tag.

@multiRename.tags.tools.name.take.description: Button in the From file name panel of the tag editor window: puts the values read from the file names into the tags. Disabled until the current pattern was previewed.

multiRename.tags.tools.name.stale: Preview again to take this pattern.

@multiRename.tags.tools.name.stale.description: Hint in the From file name panel of the tag editor window, shown after the pattern was edited since the last preview, because Take works only on a pattern that was previewed.

multiRename.tags.tools.name.previewLabel: What the pattern reads from each file name

@multiRename.tags.tools.name.previewLabe.description: Accessible name of the preview table in the From file name panel of the tag editor window.

@multiRename.tags.tools.name.columnFile.description: Column heading of the preview table in the From file name panel of the tag editor window: the file’s name.

@multiRename.tags.tools.name.columnField.description: Column heading of the preview table in the From file name panel of the tag editor window: the tag values the pattern reads from that file name.

@multiRename.tags.tools.name.noMatch.description: Cell of the preview table in the From file name panel of the tag editor window: the pattern doesn’t fit this file name, so nothing would be taken from it.

multiRename.tags.tools.name.badRegex: The pattern isn’t a valid regular expression.

@multiRename.tags.tools.name.badRegex.description: Error in the From file name panel of the tag editor window: the regular expression doesn’t compile. Nothing was changed.

@multiRename.tags.tools.name.unknownFiel.description: Error in the From file name panel of the tag editor window: the pattern names a tag field Cmdr doesn’t know. Nothing was changed.

placeholders.name: the unknown field name exactly as the user wrote it, like titel

multiRename.tags.tools.name.noFields: The pattern reads no tag field. Use a field like %title% or a named group like {example}.

@multiRename.tags.tools.name.noFields.description: Error in the From file name panel of the tag editor window: the pattern has no placeholder or named group, so there is nothing to read. The percent signs must stay as they are.

placeholders.example: a sample named group, like (?<title>.+); never translate it

multiRename.tags.numbering.title: Auto-numbering wizard

@multiRename.tags.numbering.title.description: Title of the auto-numbering dialog of the tag editor window in Multi-Rename.

@multiRename.tags.numbering.track.description: Heading of the track section of the auto-numbering dialog.

@multiRename.tags.numbering.disc.description: Checkbox heading of the disc section of the auto-numbering dialog; switching it on numbers discs too.

@multiRename.tags.numbering.begin.description: Label of the box holding the first number, in the track and the disc section of the auto-numbering dialog.

@multiRename.tags.numbering.total.description: Checkbox in the auto-numbering dialog: also write the total (the number of tracks or of discs). Switching it off removes an existing total.

@multiRename.tags.numbering.pad.description: Checkbox in the auto-numbering dialog: pad numbers with leading zeros (01, 02, …).

multiRename.tags.numbering.nextOnFolder: Next disc on change of directory

@multiRename.tags.numbering.nextOnFolder.description: Checkbox in the disc section of the auto-numbering dialog: a new disc starts where the folder changes.

@multiRename.tags.numbering.nextOnField.description: Checkbox in the disc section of the auto-numbering dialog, followed by a choice of tag field: a new disc starts where that field's first value changes.

multiRename.tags.numbering.resetTrack: Reset track counter on next disc

@multiRename.tags.numbering.resetTrack.description: Checkbox in the disc section of the auto-numbering dialog: track numbers start again at the first number on each new disc.

multiRename.tags.numbering.resetDisc: Reset disc counter on change of

@multiRename.tags.numbering.resetDisc.description: Checkbox in the disc section of the auto-numbering dialog, followed by a choice of tag field: disc numbers start again at the first number where that field's first value changes.

multiRename.tags.numbering.singleFile: A single-file book gets no track number; only the disc is numbered.

@multiRename.tags.numbering.singleFile.description: Note in the auto-numbering dialog, shown when the book has only one track.

multiRename.tags.numbering.invalidBegin: Begin at must be a whole number, 0 or more.

@multiRename.tags.numbering.invalidBegin.description: Error shown under a Begin at box of the auto-numbering dialog when it doesn't hold a whole number of at least 0.

@multiRename.tags.numbering.ok.description: Button that runs the auto-numbering dialog.

@multiRename.tags.numbering.cancel.description: Button that closes the auto-numbering dialog without numbering anything.

multiRename.tags.sort.label: Sort tracks

@multiRename.tags.sort.label.description: Screen-reader name of the row of column headers above the track list in the tag editor window; each header is a button that sorts the tracks by its column.

multiRename.tags.sort.state: {column}, {order, select, ascending {sorted ascending} descending {sorted descending} other {not sorted}}

@multiRename.tags.sort.state.description: What a screen reader says for a column header button above the track list in the tag editor window: the column’s name, then whether the tracks are sorted by it and which way, as in “Length, sorted descending” or “Title, not sorted”. Never shown on screen; the button shows only the column name and a small arrow.

placeholders.column: the column header’s own text, for example #, Title, Length, or File name
placeholders.order: ascending or descending when the tracks are sorted by this column, anything else when they aren’t

@multiRename.tags.sort.by.description: Hover tooltip on a column header above the track list in the tag editor window: clicking it puts the tracks in that column’s order (a second click reverses it).

placeholders.column: the column header’s own text, for example #, Title, Length, or File name

@multiRename.tags.col.play.description: Column header (read only by screen readers) above the play buttons in the track list of the tag editor window.

@multiRename.tags.play.failed.description: Notice in the tag editor window when a track could not be played: the file is gone, unreadable, or its format can't be played here.

@multiRename.tags.play.openInPlayer.description: Button in the tag editor window. It opens the checked tracks (or all of them when none is checked) in the foobar2000 music player when it is installed, otherwise in each file's default app.

multiRename.tags.play.playerUnavailable: Couldn’t open the tracks in a player.

@multiRename.tags.play.playerUnavailable.description: Notice in the tag editor window when Open in foobar2000 found neither foobar2000 nor any other app that could open the tracks.

multiRename.tags.play.nothingReadable: None of those tracks can be read, so none was opened.

@multiRename.tags.play.nothingReadable.description: Notice in the tag editor window when Open in foobar2000 was pressed with only unreadable tracks checked; nothing was opened.

@multiRename.tags.play.openFailed.description: Notice in the tag editor window when Open in foobar2000 failed for a reason other than a missing player, for example a track that is no longer in the list.

@multiRename.tags.openWindow.description: Button at the top of the Multi-Rename sheet (only with the opt-in tag editor setting on): opens the sheet's audio files in the Tags window, where their tags are edited. The ellipsis says it opens a window.

multiRename.tags.window.title: Tags: {folder}

@multiRename.tags.window.title.description: Title of the tag editor window. {folder} is the name of the folder the audio files are in, like "Dracula". Keep the colon between the word and the folder name.

multiRename.tags.window.nothingSelected: Select the audio files to tag first.

@multiRename.tags.window.nothingSelected.description: Notification when the user chooses Edit tags with no file selected in the file list. Nothing opens; they select the audio files, then try again.

multiRename.tags.window.openFailed: Cmdr couldn’t open these tags. Close the window and try again.

@multiRename.tags.window.openFailed.description: Shown in the tag editor window when it couldn't start (its settings didn't load). Beside a Close button.

multiRename.tags.window.bodyReloaded: The Tags window ran into a problem, so Cmdr reloaded it. Your tag edits are still here.

@multiRename.tags.window.bodyReloaded.description: Toast in the tag editor window when its content broke unexpectedly and was reloaded in place. The window stays open and the person's edits that aren't written to the files yet are kept, so they can carry on. If nothing was unwritten, the window closes instead.

@multiRename.tags.window.close.description: Button in the tag editor window that couldn't start: closes the window.

multiRename.tags.window.noTracks: None of the selected files is an audio file Cmdr can tag.

@multiRename.tags.window.noTracks.description: Notification when the user asks to edit tags but nothing selected is an audio file the tag editor supports (MP3, M4A, M4B, MP4, FLAC, OGG, Opus). No window opens.

multiRename.tags.window.tooManyTracks: Those folders hold more than {limit, number} audio files. Select a smaller part of the book.

@multiRename.tags.window.tooManyTracks.description: Notification when the user asks to edit tags on folders and the audio files in them (subfolders included) are more than the tag editor takes at once. {limit} is that most, a plain number such as 2000. No window opens.

multiRename.tags.window.foldersNeedLocal: Edit tags opens a folder only on a disk of this computer. Open the folder and select its audio files instead.

@multiRename.tags.window.foldersNeedLoca.description: Notification when the user asks to edit tags on a folder that lives on a network share, a phone or another drive Cmdr can't list the files of folder by folder; single files there still work. No window opens.

multiRename.tags.window.openTimedOut: Reading the folder took too long, so nothing was opened. Try again, or select the audio files themselves.

@multiRename.tags.window.openTimedOut.description: Notification when the user asks to edit tags on a folder and listing the audio files in it (a network share can be slow) did not finish in time. No window opens.

multiRename.tags.window.someUnreadable: {count, plural, one {# place in the folders couldn’t be read, so some tracks may be missing.} other {# places in the folders couldn’t be read, so some tracks may be missing.}}

@multiRename.tags.window.someUnreadable.description: Notification shown after the tag editor opened a folder of audio files (subfolders included) when some subfolders could not be read, so the window may lack some tracks. {count} is how many places were skipped.

multiRename.tags.keys.label: Tag tools

@multiRename.tags.keys.label.description: Accessible name of the function-key bar at the foot of the tag editor window (the separate window that edits audio files’ tags): a row of buttons, one per key (F2, F3, …), that run the tag tools.

@multiRename.tags.keys.edit.description: A button in the function-key bar at the foot of the tag editor window (the separate window that edits audio files’ tags). Shown next to its key (like F4); keep it short, one or two words, so ten buttons fit side by side. Edits the value under the cursor in place.

@multiRename.tags.keys.play.description: A button in the function-key bar at the foot of the tag editor window (the separate window that edits audio files’ tags). Shown next to its key (like F4); keep it short, one or two words, so ten buttons fit side by side. Plays or stops the track under the cursor.

@multiRename.tags.keys.replace.description: A button in the function-key bar at the foot of the tag editor window (the separate window that edits audio files’ tags). Shown next to its key (like F4); keep it short, one or two words, so ten buttons fit side by side. Opens Find and replace for tag values.

@multiRename.tags.keys.format.description: A button in the function-key bar at the foot of the tag editor window (the separate window that edits audio files’ tags). Shown next to its key (like F4); keep it short, one or two words, so ten buttons fit side by side. Opens Format a field, which rebuilds a tag field from a pattern.

@multiRename.tags.keys.fromName.description: A button in the function-key bar at the foot of the tag editor window (the separate window that edits audio files’ tags). Shown next to its key (like F4); keep it short, one or two words, so ten buttons fit side by side. Opens the dialog that reads tags out of the file names.

@multiRename.tags.keys.number.description: A button in the function-key bar at the foot of the tag editor window (the separate window that edits audio files’ tags). Shown next to its key (like F4); keep it short, one or two words, so ten buttons fit side by side. Opens the auto-numbering wizard for track numbers.

@multiRename.tags.keys.clearField.description: A button in the function-key bar at the foot of the tag editor window (the separate window that edits audio files’ tags). Shown next to its key (like F4); keep it short, one or two words, so ten buttons fit side by side. Opens a small dialog that empties one tag field.

@multiRename.tags.keys.editNumber.description: A button in the function-key bar at the foot of the tag editor window (the separate window that edits audio files’ tags). Shown next to its key (like F4); keep it short, one or two words, so ten buttons fit side by side. Shown while Shift is held. Edits the track number under the cursor. # stands for the track number.

@multiRename.tags.keys.openInPlayer.description: A button in the function-key bar at the foot of the tag editor window (the separate window that edits audio files’ tags). Shown next to its key (like F4); keep it short, one or two words, so ten buttons fit side by side. Shown while Shift is held. Opens the tracks in the foobar2000 music player.

@multiRename.tags.keys.case.description: A button in the function-key bar at the foot of the tag editor window (the separate window that edits audio files’ tags). Shown next to its key (like F4); keep it short, one or two words, so ten buttons fit side by side. Shown while Shift is held. Opens the dialog that changes a tag’s letter case.

@multiRename.tags.keys.cleanUp.description: A button in the function-key bar at the foot of the tag editor window (the separate window that edits audio files’ tags). Shown next to its key (like F4); keep it short, one or two words, so ten buttons fit side by side. Shown while Shift is held. Opens a dialog of one-press clean-up tools.

@multiRename.tags.keys.removeExtras.description: A button in the function-key bar at the foot of the tag editor window (the separate window that edits audio files’ tags). Shown next to its key (like F4); keep it short, one or two words, so ten buttons fit side by side. Shown while Shift is held. Opens the dialog that removes the files’ extra tags.

@multiRename.tags.keys.write.description: A button in the function-key bar at the foot of the tag editor window (the separate window that edits audio files’ tags). Shown next to its key (like F4); keep it short, one or two words, so ten buttons fit side by side. Writes the new tags into the files straight away.

@multiRename.tags.keys.review.description: A button in the function-key bar at the foot of the tag editor window (the separate window that edits audio files’ tags). Shown next to its key (like F4) while Shift is held, in the place of Write; keep it short, one or two words, so ten buttons fit side by side. Lists what will change in each file first, and writes on confirm.

@multiRename.tags.dialog.fromName.description: Title of the dialog in the tag editor window (the separate window that edits audio files’ tags) that reads tag values (title, track number, and so on) out of the files’ names.

@multiRename.tags.dialog.case.description: Title of the small dialog in the tag editor window (the separate window that edits audio files’ tags) that changes a tag’s letter case.

@multiRename.tags.dialog.cleanUp.description: Title of the dialog in the tag editor window (the separate window that edits audio files’ tags) holding one-press clean-up tools (remove diacritics, strip a track-number prefix, and similar).

@multiRename.tags.dialog.extras.description: Title of the dialog in the tag editor window (the separate window that edits audio files’ tags) that lists the files’ extra tags (ones not shown as fields) to pick which to remove.

@multiRename.tags.dialog.clearField.description: Title of the small dialog in the tag editor window (the separate window that edits audio files’ tags) that empties one tag field.

@multiRename.tags.dialog.write.description: Title of the dialog in the tag editor window (the separate window that edits audio files’ tags) that lists what will change in each file, then writes the new tags into the files.

@multiRename.tags.dialog.close.description: Button that closes a tool dialog in the tag editor window (the separate window that edits audio files’ tags). The tool’s own button has already applied its change; this only closes the dialog.

@multiRename.tags.clearField.field.description: Label of the drop-down that picks which tag field to empty, in the Clear a field dialog.

@multiRename.tags.clearField.all.description: What the Clear a field dialog will do when no track is selected. {field} is a tag field’s name, like Title or Album.

multiRename.tags.clearField.some: {count, plural, one {Empties {field} on the selected track.} other {Empties {field} on the {countText} selected tracks.}}

@multiRename.tags.clearField.some.description: What the Clear a field dialog will do when some tracks are selected. {field} is a tag field’s name, like Title; {countText} is the formatted number of selected tracks.

@multiRename.tags.clearField.run.description: Button in the Clear a field dialog that empties the field. Nothing is written into the files until Write.

multiRename.tags.clipboard.readFailed: Couldn’t read the clipboard. Try ⌘V again.

@multiRename.tags.clipboard.readFailed.description: Status line in the tag editor window (the separate window that edits audio files’ tags) when Command+V on a tag field couldn't read the clipboard, so nothing was pasted.

multiRename.tags.clipboard.noText: The clipboard holds no text to paste.

@multiRename.tags.clipboard.noText.description: Status line in the tag editor window when Command+V on a tag field found no plain text on the clipboard (for example, only a picture), so nothing was pasted.

multiRename.tags.clipboard.tooLong: The clipboard holds too much text for this field, so nothing was pasted.

@multiRename.tags.clipboard.tooLong.description: Status line in the tag editor window when Command+V on a tag field found more text on the clipboard than the field takes (64 KB for Comment and Description, 4 KB for the others). The field is left as it was.

multiRename.tags.clipboard.writeFailed: Couldn’t copy to the clipboard. Try again.

@multiRename.tags.clipboard.writeFailed.description: Status line in the tag editor window when Command+C or Command+X on a tag field couldn't put the field's text on the clipboard. After Command+X the field is left as it was.

@multiRename.tags.undo.editUndone.description: Status line in the tag editor window (the separate window that edits audio files’ tags) after Command+Z took back the last unwritten tag edit. One word, no detail.

@multiRename.tags.undo.editRedone.description: Status line in the tag editor window (the separate window that edits audio files’ tags) after Command+Shift+Z put back the unwritten tag edit that was just taken back. One word, no detail.

multiRename.tags.undo.nothing: There’s no tag write to undo.

@multiRename.tags.undo.nothing.description: Status line in the tag editor window (the separate window that edits audio files’ tags) when Command+Z is pressed but no tag write can be undone.

multiRename.tags.write.someLeft: Some files weren’t written. Review lists their changes again.

@multiRename.tags.write.someLeft.description: Status line in the tag editor window after the Write dialog was closed on a write that left some files unwritten (each with its reason, shown in the dialog). “Review” is the name of the function-key bar’s button that lists the changes again (multiRename.tags.keys.review).

multiRename.tags.write.doneSummary: {count, plural, one {{countText} file written} other {{countText} files written}}

@multiRename.tags.write.doneSummary.description: Status line at the foot of the tag editor window (the separate window that edits audio files’ tags) after Command+Return or Command+S wrote the new tags straight away, without listing the changes first: how many files got their new tags. Short; it goes away after a few seconds or at the next edit.

placeholders.countText: how many files were written, ready to drop into the sentence (for example 1,234)

multiRename.tags.write.doneWithProblems: {count, plural, one {{countText} file written} other {{countText} files written}}, {notWritten, plural, one {{notWrittenText} not written} other {{notWrittenText} not written}}. Review changes ({shortcut}) shows which.

@multiRename.tags.write.doneWithProblems.description: Status line at the foot of the tag editor window (the separate window that edits audio files’ tags) after Command+Return or Command+S wrote the new tags straight away and some files were left unwritten (a file that couldn’t be written, or one another app changed since it was read). “Review changes” names the command that lists the changes, files left unwritten included; keep the key in brackets as given. One line, short.

placeholders.countText: how many files were written (for example 12)
placeholders.notWrittenText: how many files were left unwritten (for example 2)
placeholders.shortcut: the key of the Review command, as the function-key bar shows it (for example ⌘⇧S); don’t translate

multiRename.tags.write.reviewRemovals: {count, plural, one {Writing as {kind} removes a tag from {countText} file, so the list shows it first.} other {Writing as {kind} removes a tag from {countText} files, so the list shows them first.}}

@multiRename.tags.write.reviewRemovals.description: Status line at the foot of the tag editor window (the separate window that edits audio files’ tags) after Command+Return or Command+S: writing as the chosen content kind would remove a tag from some files (for example an MP3’s conductor when writing as Audiobook), so nothing was written and the list of changes opened instead, naming what each file loses. The user confirms there.

placeholders.kind: the chosen content kind, as the Write dialog names it (for example Audiobook or Music)
placeholders.countText: how many files would lose a tag (for example 3)

multiRename.tags.write.listedAgain: Something changed since the list was made, so here it is again. Check it, then write.

@multiRename.tags.write.listedAgain.description: Shown in the tag editor window (the separate window that edits audio files’ tags), in its status line or next to the Write dialog’s buttons: between listing what a write will change and writing it, an edit came in or a file read differently, so files that weren’t in the list were not written and the list of changes is shown again for the user to check and confirm.

multiRename.tags.write.removesUnknown: maybe a tag it couldn’t check (removed)

@multiRename.tags.write.removesUnknown.description: Shown in the tag editor window, in the list of what a write will change in one file: the app couldn’t read the file to tell whether writing it as the chosen kind (Audiobook or Music) removes a tag, so it warns that one may be removed. One item of the list of changed fields; lower case, like “conductor (removed)”.

@multiRename.tags.write.nothingToWrite.description: Status line at the foot of the tag editor window (the separate window that edits audio files’ tags) after Command+Return or Command+S when no file’s tags would change, so nothing was written.

multiRename.tags.write.closeWaits: Writing tags… Wait until it’s done, then close the window.

@multiRename.tags.write.closeWaits.description: Shown in the tag editor window's Write dialog when the user tries to close the window (Escape, ⌘W, or the red close button) while tags are being written or undone. The window stays open so no file is left half written; once the write ends, the dialog shows what it did and the window can be closed.

multiRename.tags.window.closeWaits: Writing tags… Wait until it’s done, then close the window.

@multiRename.tags.window.closeWaits.description: Shown in the tag editor window's status line when the user tries to close the window while tags are being written or undone. Same meaning as the Write dialog's line: the window stays open until the write ends.

multiRename.tags.readTimedOut: The drive stopped answering while the tags were read. Close the window and try again.

@multiRename.tags.readTimedOut.description: Shown in the tag editor window instead of the tracks when reading the files' tags stood still for a while, usually because a network drive stopped answering. Nothing was changed.

multiRename.tags.quit.title: {count, plural, one {Quit with tag changes not written?} other {Quit with tag changes not written in {countText} windows?}}

@multiRename.tags.quit.title.description: Title of the quit dialog when the only thing holding the quit is one or more tag editor windows (Edit tags) whose changes haven't been written into the files yet. Quitting discards those changes.

placeholders.count: how many tag editor windows hold unwritten changes (drives the singular/plural form)
placeholders.countText: the same count, already formatted with the locale’s digit grouping

multiRename.tags.quit.writingTitle: Quit while tags are being written?

@multiRename.tags.quit.writingTitle.description: Title of the quit dialog when the only thing holding the quit is a tag editor window writing tags into files right now.

multiRename.tags.quit.unwritten: {count, plural, one {A Tags window has changes that haven’t been written. Quitting discards them.} other {{countText} Tags windows have changes that haven’t been written. Quitting discards them.}}

@multiRename.tags.quit.unwritten.description: A line in the quit dialog: tag editor windows (titled "Tags") hold tag changes not yet written into the files, and quitting loses them. Choosing "Keep working" keeps them.

placeholders.count: how many tag editor windows hold unwritten changes (drives the singular/plural form)
placeholders.countText: the same count, already formatted with the locale’s digit grouping

multiRename.tags.quit.writing: Tags are being written. Cmdr finishes writing them before it quits, so no book is left half written.

@multiRename.tags.quit.writing.description: A line in the quit dialog: a tag editor window is writing tags into audio files right now. Cmdr waits for that write to end before quitting (up to a short limit), rather than stopping between files. "Book" means an audiobook, a folder of audio files.

multiRename.tags.quit.waits: Cmdr waits for your answer, so no tag changes are lost while you’re away.

@multiRename.tags.quit.waits.description: A line at the foot of the quit dialog, in place of its usual countdown, when the only thing holding the quit is tag changes not yet written in tag editor windows. Cmdr doesn't quit on its own then: it waits until the user picks Quit now or Keep working.

@multiRename.tags.write.sideHeading.description: Shown in the tag editor window: heading of the part of the list of changes about the small text files Cmdr writes into the book folder for the Audiobookshelf app (reader.txt, desc.txt).

@multiRename.tags.write.sideCreate.description: Shown in the tag editor window's list of changes, under the files: a text file that doesn't exist yet will be created with this text. {fileName} is reader.txt or desc.txt.

placeholders.fileName: the side file’s name, reader.txt or desc.txt
placeholders.text: what the file will say (a narrator’s name, or the book’s description)

@multiRename.tags.write.sideReplace.description: Shown in the tag editor window's list of changes, under the files: a text file there says something else and will be replaced. {old} is what it says now, {text} what it will say.

placeholders.fileName: the side file’s name, reader.txt or desc.txt

@multiRename.tags.write.sideWithheld.description: Shown in the tag editor window's list of changes, under the files: a text file Cmdr won't write, and why ({reason} is one of the multiRename.tags.write.sideWhy.* texts).

placeholders.fileName: the side file’s name, reader.txt or desc.txt
placeholders.reason: why, one of the multiRename.tags.write.sideWhy.* texts

@multiRename.tags.write.sideWhy.readerDi.description: Why reader.txt isn't written: the tracks' Performer (narrator) values differ. Completes multiRename.tags.write.sideWithheld.

@multiRename.tags.write.sideWhy.descDisa.description: Why desc.txt isn't written: the tracks' Description values differ. Completes multiRename.tags.write.sideWithheld.

multiRename.tags.write.sideWhy.tooLong: its text is longer than 64 KB

@multiRename.tags.write.sideWhy.tooLong.description: Why a side text file isn't written: the text is too long. Completes multiRename.tags.write.sideWithheld.

multiRename.tags.write.sideWhy.notAFile: something other than a plain file has that name

@multiRename.tags.write.sideWhy.notAFile.description: Why a side text file isn't written: a link or a folder has its name, and Cmdr never writes through it. Completes multiRename.tags.write.sideWithheld.

multiRename.tags.write.sideWhy.unreadabl: the file there can’t be read, so it couldn’t be put back

@multiRename.tags.write.sideWhy.unreadab.description: Why a side text file isn't written: the existing one is too large or unreadable, so Undo couldn't restore it. Completes multiRename.tags.write.sideWithheld.

multiRename.tags.write.sideWhy.notOneBoo: the tracks come from more than one book folder

@multiRename.tags.write.sideWhy.notOneBo.description: Why a side text file isn't written: the opened tracks sit in several book folders (two folders, or a folder and loose files), so there's no one folder to put it in. Completes multiRename.tags.write.sideWithheld.

@multiRename.tags.write.sideWritten.description: Shown in the tag editor window after a write: the small text files (reader.txt, desc.txt) it also wrote into the book folder. {files} is a list of file names.

placeholders.files: the file names, as a list (for example reader.txt and desc.txt)

@multiRename.tags.write.sideNotWrittenHe.description: Shown in the tag editor window after a write: heading of the list of side text files (reader.txt, desc.txt) it didn't write: one that says something else and wasn't shown in the list of changes, or one that couldn't be written.

multiRename.tags.write.reviewSideFiles: {count, plural, one {A file beside the book says something else, so the list shows its replacement first.} other {Files beside the book say something else, so the list shows their replacement first.}}

@multiRename.tags.write.reviewSideFiles.description: Status line at the foot of the tag editor window after Command+Return or Command+S: reader.txt or desc.txt in the book folder already says something else, so it wasn't replaced and the list of changes opened instead, showing the old and the new text. The user confirms there.

placeholders.countText: how many files, ready to drop into the sentence
